correctness.rationale: A complete analytic proof derives alias-class cancellation from finite-group Fourier inversion, a sharp zero-sum weighted ℓ1/ℓ2 inequality with two-frequency rigidity, and an orthogonal sum estimate. Product weights reduce every minimizing alias to one axis; strict convexity/concavity identifies all r<1, r=1, r>1 regimes. Explicit witnesses attain the bounds. The diameter and reconstruction statements follow by central symmetry and triangle inequality; the comparison invokes verified Theorem 7.4 of arXiv:2611.12558. The 9,029 test assertions are finite corroboration, not evidence for the infinite claim.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary 2026 Gelfand/sampling-width papers optimize over sample designs and establish asymptotic rates, whereas this theorem is a fixed-grid exact nullspace norm and complete alias-frequency classification at every m and r, with a nondifferentiable smoothness-one transition. The relevant 2023 sparse-grid approximation theorems concern operator errors/asymptotics, not this sharp two-mode zero-fiber invariant. Explicit searches of published mathematical records across aliases, frequencies, weighted ℓ1 kernels and exact tables yielded related but non-covering spectral/sampling records. Acknowledged classical Fourier aliasing alone does not state the sharp weighted radius, equality and product-grid law; unindexed prior equivalence remains a risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed earlier sampling/aliasing results or textbook exercises might contain an equivalent fixed-grid radius formula; database and literature searches cannot certify first priority.
